question.text: Under the RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), a resident Indian investor can remit up to USD _______ per person per financial year for permissible current and capital account transactions including investment in an offshore fund.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** LRS allows resident Indians to remit up to USD 2,50,000 per person per financial year for any permissible current or capital account transaction (or combination) subject to FEMA conditions. This is the cap when resident Indians invest in offshore funds. **The Trap:** USD 50,000 and USD 1,00,000 were earlier ceilings that have since been revised. USD 5,00,000 is fabricated. The current figure in the workbook is USD 2,50,000. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B/C/D all test LRS cap. Retail-facing X-A/X-B also touches it for investment-advisory clients. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When your Cat III onshore fund runs out of capacity and you push resident HNIs to an offshore feeder, each investor can only route USD 2.5 lakh per year via LRS — do the math before marketing such a structure.
